summary: 1 selected Alignment image; Six Crab Nebula views compare optical line emission, near/mid-infrared components, radio synchrotron and the X-ray pulsar wind on a shared sky frame. Different epochs, passbands and resolutions produce real morphological differences; alignment must not erase expansion or force different emission mechanisms into agreement.

images.wavelengths: Optical · [O III] 502 nm / [O I] 631 nm / [S II] 673 nm
images.coverage: Main optical remnant, 6.41′ square; the faint northern ejecta jet is outside this tight presentation footprint.
images.quality: Detailed emission-line mosaic; RGB intensity mixes species, ionization and display stretch. Final composite PSF is not specified.
notes: Eight-field observation interval is documented in Dubner et al. §V: https://arxiv.org/html/1704.02968v1
Publisher AVM has a full TAN solution attributed to NASA/Hubble. Field-star residuals must establish independent registration quality.

images.coverage: Main remnant, 5.47′ × 4.76′; tight common mosaic crop, with emission approaching the edges. No faint northern-jet coverage.
images.quality: Official 4000-pixel publication TIFF, preserving the full master footprint. Broad filters mix synchrotron, lines and dust; not a calibrated spectral cube.
notes: AVM quality is Position, not Full: complete numerical WCS is supplied, but publisher accuracy remains provisional.
Master grid is 10509 × 9151; preserve its AVM reference pixels when using the 4000 × 3483 derivative.
Publisher PAH/silicate band labels are not evidence of pure PAH or silicate emission.

images.coverage: Main remnant, 5.33′ × 4.62′; tight crop. No faint northern-jet coverage.
images.quality: Derived component display: synchrotron blue, sulfur green, dust magenta. Shares Webb observations with the infrared composite; not independent evidence or a dust-density map.
notes: Full TAN AVM retained; component subtraction makes field-star matching unsuitable as a required registration test.
Component isolation depends on subtraction and PSF matching: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.00172v1

images.coverage: 8.83′ square presentation field around the main remnant; diffuse infrared filaments are broad at this resolution.
images.quality: Single-band false-color display, strongly oversampled; final PSF and noise map are not supplied. No photometry or upper limits from black pixels.
images.epoch: Observation date unspecified in the selected release; released 2017-05-15.
notes: Selected ESA/Hubble release omits instrument/filter tags. MIPS and 24 µm come from the linked CXC companion TIFF AVM, not a measured spectrum: https://chandra.harvard.edu/photo/2017/crab/more.html
Treat line emission, synchrotron and dust as possible contributors; infrared brightness alone is not dust mass.
Full TAN publisher WCS retained without fitting the nebular structure.

images.telescope: Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array
images.wavelengths: Radio · S band, approximately 3 GHz / 10 cm
images.coverage: 8.83′ square field containing the extended radio remnant. Fine radio filaments and diffuse synchrotron occupy a larger region than bright X-rays.
images.quality: Genuine interferometric radio map rendered in red. Published parent map beam is 0.93″ × 0.80″; which large-scale weighting this outreach rendering uses is unspecified.
images.epoch: VLA 2012-11-26 and 2012-11-27; historical 5 GHz template supplies large scales. Released 2017-05-15.
notes: Parent map combines S-band data with an expanded, spectrally scaled older template; an additional high-pass version exists: https://arxiv.org/html/1704.02968v1
Not a flux-calibrated TIFF. Do not interpret a narrow display pixel or missing smooth emission as instrumental resolution or physical absence.
Full TAN publisher WCS retained; radio wisps must not be forced onto optical features.

images.wavelengths: X-ray · ACIS; exact selected display passband unspecified
images.coverage: 8.83′ square field; detected X-ray pulsar-wind emission is intrinsically concentrated on the inner torus and jets, not the full optical ejecta envelope.
images.quality: Single-band false-color display. Final stacked PSF, exposure map and band limits are absent from the selected image metadata; not a temperature or density map.
images.epoch: Companion CXC release lists 48 pointings, March 2000–November 2013; exact selected stack membership unspecified. Released 2017-05-15.
notes: CXC AVM central wavelength 0.8267 nm is a representative display tag, not an energy-band definition.
The companion paper’s near-contemporaneous 2012 exposure must not be substituted for the release stack epoch.
Full TAN publisher WCS retained; compact torus morphology is not a field-star registration reference.

papers.title: Dubner et al. — Morphological properties of the Crab Nebula: a detailed multiwavelength study
papers.access: Open author manuscript and HTML; observational setup and parent maps are described. Quantitative work needs calibrated data, not the outreach TIFFs.
constraints: Radio and optical/X-ray wisps need not coincide, even near the same epoch. Register sky coordinates rather than emission peaks.
VLA large-scale structure includes a transformed older template; separate that processing from current observations.

papers.title: Temim et al. — Dissecting the Crab Nebula with JWST
papers.access: Open paper; program 1714 data at https://doi.org/10.17909/6264-w578.
constraints: NIRCam scientific pixel grids are 0.031″ and 0.063″; MIRI grid is 0.11″. These differ from delivered display sampling and resolution.
Adopted PSF FWHM varies from 0.055″ at 1.62 µm to 0.674″ at 21 µm; match PSFs before comparing fine features.
Two MIRI spectroscopy fields do not measure abundances everywhere. Component subtraction assumptions constrain dust interpretation.

papers.title: Martin, Milisavljevic & Drissen — 3D mapping of the Crab Nebula with SITELLE – I. Deconvolution and kinematic reconstruction
papers.access: Open journal article; author manuscript at https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.02709. No spectral cube acquired for this Alignment intake.
constraints: Hα, [N II] and [S II] Doppler components constrain emitting gas. Depth follows an assumed expansion relation, not image brightness.
Uniform global expansion is a model approximation; the ejecta envelope is not adequately represented by a simple ellipsoid.

papers.title: Martin et al. — The non-uniform expansion of the Crab Nebula
papers.access: Open author manuscript: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.19632. CFHT images at 2007, 2016 and 2019 underpin the motion measurements.
constraints: Spatially varying proper motions and acceleration invalidate a single affine expansion correction for all filaments.
Use field stars or qualified publisher WCS for astrometry; preserve epoch differences as physical information.

papers.title: Ding et al. — 3D Kinematic Reconstruction of the Crab Nebula That Includes the Northern Ejecta Jet
papers.access: Open author manuscript and HTML; CFHT/SITELLE programs 20BC02 and 22BD14. Data cubes were not acquired here.
constraints: 2020 and 2022 spectral observations add [O III] and other tracers; red-line-only coverage misses much of the northern jet.
Line-of-sight distance depends on expansion and assumed distance; source selection and flux thresholds affect the displayed structure.
The faint northern ejecta jet is different from the inner X-ray pulsar jet and is not fully covered by the selected tight optical/Webb mosaics.

selection.reason: Optical reference retained. Webb and other spectral views remain documented but hidden until their independent sky alignment can be established; publisher placement alone is not enough.
